title: Lists, dictionaries & sets
outcome: Model device data and transform it without accidental information loss.

steps.title: 1. Choose a representation
steps.text: Lists preserve order and duplicates. Dictionaries map unique keys to values. Sets store unique hashable values. Choose based on the required operation.

steps.title: 2. Avoid silent overwrites
steps.text: Building a dictionary keyed by ID overwrites an earlier duplicate unless you detect it. Decide whether duplicates are invalid, grouped, or replaced.

steps.title: 3. Separate required and optional
steps.text: d[key] requires a key; d.get(key, default) handles an absent key. An existing None is not automatically replaced by that default.

steps.title: 4. Normalize only what is intended
steps.text: Do not silently lowercase case-sensitive identifiers. Include a routing context in composite keys when addresses can legitimately repeat between contexts.

steps.title: 5. Test duplicates and ordering
steps.text: A set operation often needs explicit sorting before a deterministic report. Avoid modifying caller data unless the contract asks for it.
